rationale: I re-read the genuine decision. Its bytes hash to fd16cbbb..., the same bytes as STATUS_DECISION.producer.json. The ACT and ACTOR_TEXT spans match the bytes exactly. Identity is confirmed: 23 FR 5061, July 1, 1958, 'Delegating and Transferring Certain Functions and Affairs to the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization'. Secs. 1-4 define the ODCM, delegate the Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958 functions, redelegate earlier ODM/FCDA functions, and amend references in listed prior orders. The held text is truncated at '(Continued on p. 5063)', so sec. 7 and the later sections are not held, as the producer discloses. Its only savings parenthetical is on item (7), EO 10539. The 'to the extent' qualifier saves nothing; it reaches whatever had not already been displaced. So the machine 'partial' scope label does not defeat a whole-order end of everything remaining. The FR ACTOR_TEXT corroborates the mirror ACT record. I checked the other actors. EO 10782 amends the order. EO 10952 sec. 7 amends 10773 'accordingly'. EO 10958 supersedes prior orders including 10773 only to the extent of its scope. EO 12148 5-101 revokes only EO 10242. EO 10838, 10901-10903 and 10941 merely cite the order. The cruden number search (19 hits) found no other whole ending and no revival after 1962. The flag PARTIAL_OR_QUALIFIED_CHANGE_REQUIRES_CLAUSE_CHECK is honestly resolved, and the identity, earlier-ending, partial-scope and savings flags are true of the sources. The NO is therefore supported as a nonauthoritative provisional proposal. Lifecycle gaps remain. Sections after p. 5062 are unread, so the clause inventory is incomplete and an unseen own-term or savings provision cannot be excluded. No effective date for EO 11051 is held, and signing is not an effective end. The first-effective cessation of individual functions through EO 10952/10958 has not been reconciled. No complete later-source search through 2026-10-14 has been done. Pages were not image-checked (original_pages_confirmed false). No owner adoption or human certification follows.
